t:
(a) In General.—Section 514(c)(9)(C) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “or” after clause (ii), by striking the period at the end of clause (iii) and inserting “; or”, and by inserting after clause (iii) the following:“(iv) a retirement income account described in section 403(b)(9).”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to taxable years beginning on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only amends Internal Revenue Code section 514(c)(9)(C) to add church retirement income accounts under section 403(b)(9) as qualified organizations, and sets an effective date. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to add retirement income accounts to a list in section 514(c)(9)(C), and it sets an effective date. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Mentioning private retirement accounts only defines who the provision covers; it does not bring outsiders into a federal decision.
opus.s: "(iv) a retirement income account described in section 403(b)(9)."

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to include a specific type of retirement income account. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory committees, or hearings. The text is purely legislative and procedural regarding the effective date of the amendment, with no involvement of non-federal parties in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the tax code affects the public, but the text itself does not describe any process for public input, consultation, or participation. It is purely a legislative amendment to a statute.
